newsitem.title: USA: Japan economy growing slowly, steadily - MOF official.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy growing slowly, steadily - MOF official.

text.p: A senior Japanese official Tuesday declared the Japanese economy is recovering slowly and steadily, and said he was not concerned about the possibility that the U.S. Federal Reserve might raise interest rates.
But Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of the Ministry of Finance's International Finance Bureau, declined to comment at a news conference on current exchange rate levels.
The dollar has gained ground recently against the Japanese yen, aided by growing expectations of higher U.S. interest rates and by Monday's U.S. cruise missile attack on Iraq.
Sakakibara declined to say whether he thought the dollar could rise further.
Asked about previous comments attributed to him suggesting that the dollar could rise to 120 yen, Sakakibara replied, "That was misreported."
He acknowledged that there was "some perception" in the financial markets that the Fed might raise interest rates next month, but argued that it was not widespread.
"I am not in a position to comment on that," Sakakibara said. "But if you ask am I concerned about it or not, I am not concerned about it."
He said that Japan's economy was recovering slowly, and noted that last week's (Tankan) report on business sentiment by the Bank of Japan was not as good as expected.
"We are on a steady, slow recovery path," he said.
Sakakibara effectively declined commment on whether Japan would introduce a supplementary budget to help keep its economic expansion on track.
"A Ministry of Finance official would never say until the last moment that a supplementary budget is needed," Sakakibara said.
He said he had been on vacation and thus would refrain from commenting on reports that Japan had decided not to submit a supplementary budget.

Sakakibara, who attended an Inter-American Development Bank conference here, was not optimistic about the chances of the United States and Japan settling their differences over the deregulation of Japan's lucrative insurance market.
Sakakibara said he hoped to resolve those differences. But he added, "I am not optimistic."
He said he might briefly meet U.S. trade negotiator Ira Shapiro while in Washington. But he said he did not intend to negotiate on the insurance issue at this time.
The Japanese official is also scheduled to meet Deputy U.S. Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers today before departing from Washington Wednesday.
